question: Can a free, continuously open cloud browser directly and reliably detect Pokemon Center Germany queues without the user's PC or credits?
outcome: Cloud browser hosting is possible within some free VM allocations, but direct Germany access has not been demonstrated. A single ordinary headed Chrome tab on a GitHub Linux runner stayed blocked during a five-minute session. No new production browser monitor enabled.

live_test.runtime: GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04, headed Chrome under Xvfb, one context and tab
live_test.interpretation: Twelve DOM observations of the same HTTP 403 document; one main-document response, not twelve requests. No readable store or German queue. COMPLETE/success means diagnostic completion only.

hosting_review.verdict: Not sufficient for a continuously open browser: 240 minutes needed for 16:00-20:00, 1440 minutes for 24h. No deployment or existing shared-budget change.

hosting_review.free_limit: Always Free VMs in home region, including up to two AMD micro instances or aggregate A1 Flex allocation of 1500 OCPU hours and 9000 GB hours/month (2 OCPU/12GB equivalent according to current docs).
caveats: Idle instances may be reclaimed; no uptime SLA.
Account setup requires identity/payment-card verification; Always Free differs from the expiring trial credit.
hosting_review.verdict: Potential credit-free persistent host, not a verified Pokemon Center transport. User confirmed no Oracle Cloud account exists; no Oracle access test or new infrastructure.

hosting_review.free_limit: Standard runners are free for public repositories; a GitHub-hosted job is limited to six hours and jobs use fresh runner VMs.
hosting_review.verdict: Used only for this bounded diagnostic. No uninterrupted 24/7 browser service; current access test failed.

hosting_review.free_limit: Free web services, 750 instance hours/month; spin down after 15 minutes without inbound traffic.
hosting_review.verdict: Not a reliable always-running free background-browser host; restarts/spindown lose local files. No account or keepalive workaround configured.

hosting_review.free_limit: 1000 units/month; each 30 seconds of open browser time consumes one unit, including idle time.
hosting_review.verdict: At most 500 browser minutes/month before other consumption; still quota-based and insufficient for the requested continuous watch.

local_suite.skip_reason: Browser-dependent tests require a browser runtime; existing visible-DOM tests ran separately in the cloud.

validation.limits: A five-minute negative result on one GitHub runner does not establish that every cloud network is blocked. Synthetic Germany queue fixtures validate classification only.
